_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282. Press 4.34.0 generates doctorBaseURLIsPlaceholder in doctor.go and resolves {datacenter} from config before the placeholder check (doctorBase), so the asserts follow the generated shape. Press 4.34.0 fills an unset datacenter with eu2-cloud, so the resolved base no longer looks like a placeholder and doctor reported a host the operator never chose as their API; doctor now reports 'not configured (no datacenter chosen)' naming ACRONIS_DATACENTER and ACRONIS_BASE_URL unless the datacenter came from the environment or the config file (config.DatacenterChosen).

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For acronis the manifest gained: ACRONIS_BASE_URL, ACRONIS_CLIENT_ID, ACRONIS_CLIENT_SECRET. server.json gained: ACRONIS_BASE_URL, ACRONIS_BEARER_AUTH, ACRONIS_CLIENT_ID, ACRONIS_CLIENT_SECRET. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: ACRONIS_BASE_URL, ACRONIS_CLIENT_ID, ACRONIS_CLIENT_SECRET. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.why: Issue #325 exposed missing sync resources and unsupported parameters. Preserve the official API mappings and fixture-tested completeness gate when regenerating.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 1 command listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs it
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: agent-manager force-agent-update (POST /api/agent_manager/v2/agents/update:force).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown). `auth login` (internal/cli/acronis_auth_login.go) funnels the token endpoint's error body and its no-access_token answer with the client secret it sent (an echo of the Basic value decodes to it). Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts. Press 4.34.0 surfaces (endpoint usage and sync_error envelopes, async job pending error, permission envelope, force-agent-update per-item error) pass funnelShownError too (cli-factory acronis/reapply/funnel_envelopes.py).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

handfixes.summary: On press 4.34.0 the Acronis sync keeps the 4.24 partition contract (task-manager = tasks, agent-manager = agents, usages and offering_items as tenant dependents), fails a resource whose flat walk is incomplete for any reason, scopes to the root tenant except under the verifier waiver, and UpsertBatch reports typed projection failures instead of swallowing them.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 renamed the tasks partition to task-manager-v2-tasks, moved activities onto task-manager (which feeds the task_manager rollup table) and turned agents into a per-tenant api_agent_manager_v2_agents dependent; every rollup would have read activities as tasks and an empty agent table. 4.34.0 also let a max_pages_cap stop pass as a warning and UpsertBatch drop typed projection failures, so an incomplete mirror could drive failures, health and drift rollups. All edits are in generated files (sync.go, store.go, promoted_remote-search.go, task-manager_list-activities.go); a reprint reverts them while go build and go test stay green. Re-apply scripts: cli-factory acronis/reapply/resource_names.py, sync_contract.py, store_typed_failures.py.

handfixes.summary: appendRecipeStringFlag in internal/mcp/intents.go always emits one --name=value element; the generated useEquals=false split branch (--name, value as two elements) is removed.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 (#5045) places a flag-like recipe positional after --, which retired the positional half of mcp-recipe-argv-not-flag-like, but its appendRecipeStringFlag still emits --name and the value as two argv elements when useEquals is false. Joined, a value can never be read as a second flag, whatever the target flag's type. A reprint restores the split branch while go build and go test stay green.

handfixes.summary: The clients get / clients delete examples and pp:happy-args use the low-entropy placeholder 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 instead of the spec's random-looking client UUID.
handfixes.why: gitleaks' generic-api-key rule reads `clients get <random uuid>` as a client secret, so the fleet gitleaks gate fails on the generated example. The spec example comes from the 4.34.0 reprint's path-param examples; the press emits it verbatim into clients_get.go, clients_delete.go and the MCP tool descriptions, so a reprint restores it. spec-encode: use a low-entropy client_id example in the library spec.

handfixes.summary: Every template value substituted into the base URL's host (today {datacenter}) must be one ASCII DNS label; buildURL refuses anything else before substitution, and auth login's datacenter check uses the same validator.
handfixes.why: The base URL is https://{datacenter}.acronis.com and the client attaches the Authorization header to whatever host it builds. Before this, a datacenter value such as sink.example/ (from ACRONIS_DATACENTER, the config file, or an MCP sync call's path-context argument) built https://sink.example/.acronis.com and sent the MSP's token there. buildURL is generated (internal/client/url.go), so a reprint drops the check while go build and go test stay green.

handfixes.summary: Credentials that arrive in a request (a client secret passed to idp request-token, a token passed to idp revoke-token, any credential-named query or body field) are recorded with the process-wide secret funnel before the request is sent, so a server answer repeating them is withheld from CLI errors and MCP tool results.
handfixes.why: The funnel held only the configured credentials. `idp request-token --client-secret S` against a 400 answer that repeated S printed S in the --json error envelope, on stderr and in the MCP tool error. On the identity provider's endpoints every request string is held; elsewhere a value is held when its field name reads as a credential. doInternal is generated (internal/client/client.go), so a reprint drops the call. A JSON body is decoded with numbers kept as written, so a numeric credential is held in the digits sent (a number under a credential-named field was not held).

handfixes.summary: A credential an Acronis API response carries never reaches disk: every store write choke point (resources.data, each typed table's data and columns, resources_fts, row identity) drops credential-named fields via the shared cliutil.IsSecretField predicate, clients.client_secret is always NULL, the idp resource type (token answers) is refused whole, and the HTTP response cache and the file cache refuse any body carrying a credential field or coming from an /idp/ path. The request-credential detector now uses the same shared predicate and keeps every signal it had.
handfixes.why: clients create answers 201 with client_secret (Acronis account-management OpenAPI); writeMutationResponseToStore wrote it through UpsertBatch into resources.data, the typed clients.client_secret column and FTS, where the MCP sql and search tools and any local reader see it. An idp token answer that carried an identity field was stored the same way (access and refresh tokens in resources and the typed idp columns), a GET answer with a nested password or client secret was written to both the store (write-through) and the on-disk response cache, and a row whose only identity field was named like a credential (key) used the secret as resources.id. store.go, client.go and cache.go are generated, so a reprint drops every guard while go build and go test stay green. Ported from the servosity precedent (secret-family-never-persisted); a field named exactly code keeps a digit-free word value because Acronis task rows carry result.code ok/error, which the task_manager.result_code column reads. Stores written by an earlier release are not purged (accepted risk). Every store write (Upsert, UpsertBatch, UpsertBatchDetailed and each typed Upsert*) cleans the whole incoming row once at its entry (cleanIncomingRow), before identity resolution or envelope unwrapping, so a credential-named wrapper such as {"password":{"id":...,"value":...}} can no longer be unwrapped into the stored row; plural and credential names (passwords, secrets, tokens, api_keys, apikeys, private_keys, credential, credentials) match at any depth, and a bare number under a plural name is a count, not a credential. A response is also cleaned whole before any envelope is unwrapped on the way to the store (write-through and mutation answers), and no sole-collection fallback (write-through, pagination, sync, the map-keyed flattener) unwraps rows from under a credential-named key: write-through picked the only array in {"tokens":[...]} as the rows, and the row clean never saw the wrapper name.

handfixes.summary: One endpoint-to-partition table (acronis_contract.go acronisPartitionEndpoints) picks the local partition of every store read and write outside sync: the read resolvers, their local fallback, write-through and mutation answers. An endpoint that feeds no mirrored partition (hardware nodes, agent update settings, agents/update:force) gets none: nothing is written and no local read answers it.
handfixes.why: The generated read resolvers and writeMutationResponseToStore used the command's label, so task-manager get-activity wrote an Acronis Activity (Task Manager API Activity schema) into the tasks partition that failures and health read, and hardware-node reads and agent mutations wrote into the agents partition. The resolvers, writeThroughCache, resolveLocal and writeMutationResponseToStore are generated (internal/cli/data_source.go) and so are the nine mutation callers that now pass their path, so a reprint drops the routing; a reprint that drops the path argument fails to compile.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #4647: every value-carrying branch of cliArgsFromMCP joins the value to its flag (--k=v, one element per list item), and the press generates TestCliArgsFromMCP_ValueCannotSmuggleBlockedFlag.
tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Upstreamed as cli-printing-press #5045 (4.33.6): a recipe positional that looks like a flag is placed after --, so it cannot set another flag.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: The note paused HTTP mode until a reprint because the build served HTTP with no token. Press 4.34.0 HTTP mode refuses to start without <PREFIX>_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN, answers 401 without the right bearer, binds 127.0.0.1 by default and refuses a non-loopback address without TLS; onboard.py now writes HTTP guidance that follows the binary (cc-skills #14) and never writes this note, so the entry would fail on every re-onboard.

tools/maintainer/fleet_handfixes.json: Press 4.34.0's cobratree mirror derives one blocked set per command (destination, input, mcp:write-flags, mcp:read-flags and root control-plane flags), leaves those flags out of the tool schema and refuses them, and any undeclared argument, by name.
